notes.shellfish_allergy: Deborah is allergic to shellfish; no shellfish in any shared meal even where it would score well for El Hachemi. Shell-free fish (sea bream, hake, sea bass, mackerel) substituted.
notes.halal: No pork in any meal, individual or shared, even though pork scores well in both reports. Mutton used instead (scores 9 for El Hachemi same dishes).
notes.rationale_intro: You've told us the gas and heavy digestion you feel after eating seem 'normal', but your report points to some concrete causes: your protein metabolism is low, your Akkermansia is well below the community average (a key bacteria for gut wall health), and your microbial diversity is low. On weight: your metabolic score (45) is higher than you'd like, mostly because your sugar and processed-food index are also elevated. Your already-good fat metabolism is a point in your favor.

phases.blurb_en: We immediately remove every food that scores 0-3 for either of you. Simple, well-cooked meals, with easy-to-digest proteins (lamb, chicken, white fish) and moderate portions, designed to ease El Hachemi's heavy digestion and start working on Deborah's metabolic score without sudden changes.

general_notes: Shellfish is always excluded because of Deborah's allergy, even though it scores well in her report; a score never overrides a known allergy.
Pork is always excluded by the family's halal practice, even though it scores well in both reports; mutton is used instead and scores just as well for both of you.
Prioritize small wild-caught fish (sardine, anchovy, mackerel, herring) over farmed fish, and mineral water over tap water, to help bring down Deborah's antibiotic damage.
Cook vegetables and legumes thoroughly before eating them; this especially helps your digestion, given your low protein metabolism score.
Season shared meals with garlic, spring onion, shallot, fresh herbs and salt instead of onion, tomato, ginger and cinnamon, since these score low for at least one of you.
Aim for at least one serving of sauerkraut a day from week 3 onward to help rebuild diversity for both of you.
This plan is a framework, not a rule. If either of you notices a food marked 'enrich' doesn't sit well, drop it regardless of its score.
This plan complements any medication Deborah is taking; any meal-timing schedule set by her doctor or pharmacist stays exactly as advised.

Check back in on how you're both feeling after week 6: digestion, energy and knee pain. A full microbiome re-test happens once a year to keep the gut healthy and balanced; these 6 weeks are about planting the right seeds, not about seeing measurable changes in the microbiome itself just yet.
